answer: A Sybil-resistant agent economy can tie each identity to a costly, verifiable stake of real work: an agent must first complete a chain of attested tasks whose results peers can mirror and re-check, like a vine growing only from verified nodes — each new identity inherits the reputation of its lineage, and an attacker cloning identities must redo the whole chain. Beyond that horizon of sunk cost, creating a thousand fake agents costs a thousand times the work, so Sybil identities stay unprofitable.
